Both men talk of Russia as a potential partner and approach the country as businessmen who, like Trump, seek “win-win” solutions with Putin.

CNN’s Fareed Zakaria says there’s one big problem with that strategy. Also, he talks to Polish Deputy Prime Minister Radoslaw Sikorski who argues that Putin has “been at war with us for a decade”.

author: CNN
description:
Gulf diplomats and Iranian officials were set to meet Monday to discuss an Omani plan for reopening the Strait of Hormuz to regular tanker traffic, a conversation that would have happened without a critical player: the United States.

But, as news of the meeting circulated on Sunday, it was indefinitely postponed, according to the Omani foreign minister.
After months of private discussions on a complicated possible legal framework to reopen the strait that could allow Iran and Oman to collect fees, diplomats hoped the gathering could create some momentum for a deal.

Saudi Arabia submitted amendments because it had concerns that the proposed language could effectively establish a new status quo that would not be acceptable to it or the other Gulf Cooperation Council states.

description:
The American airman rescued from Iran after his aircraft was shot down in April shared for the first time details about the risky recovery operation during a “60 Minutes” interview Sunday. “Bravo,” the airman’s mission call sign used during the broadcast to shield his identity, said his parachute was damaged after the plane was hit, and that during free fall, he did everything he could to “unfurl or pull pieces of the parachute loose.”

CNN reported Saturday that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and political appointees in his department pushed for the two crew members to participate in the exclusively and highly publicized interview, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.

CNN talks to retired Air Force Colonel Cedric Leighton about the rescue & potential risks to “Bravo” in Iran after his TV appearance and CNN’s chief media analyst Brian Stelter reveals how Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth & the Pentagon made this interview happen.

author: CNN
description:
A remarkable sequence of warnings by leaders of artificial intelligence firms that their creation may soon outpace humans’ capacity to control it has so far been met with a shrug by Republicans who run Washington.

President Donald Trump said Sunday that “negative forces” were conjuring up “things that won’t happen.” House Speaker Mike Johnson rejected a call to pass emergency legislation, telling CNN’s Jake Tapper that AI executives “pushing the frontier” could slow down if they wanted, but Congress shouldn’t rush to act.
While Democrats are trying to put this issue front and center for the upcoming midterms as GA Senator Jon Ossoff blames Trump as being “compromised” on AI policy.
